messages.subject: Using Inla with SPDE approach
parts:
Hello 

I got in a trouble, so i appreciate you if give me a hint

I am studding spatio-temporal data and i am using INLA and SPDE approach

My question is:

when i want to predict response in some new locations (for example on a grid) and i don't have the values of covariates at those locations,
what should i do?

 In the blue part below, i should have a data frame of covariates with dimention= (number of points for prediction)*(number of covariates),  but it is not possible to have it? How can i do prediction and enter the effect of covariates?

A_pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh,
                      loc=as.matrix(pred.grid),                          # pred.grid : is a grid for prediction
                      group=i_day,                                             # i_day : selected day for prediction
                      n.group=n_days)


stack_pred <- inla.stack(data=list(y=NA),
                         A=list(A_pred,1),
                         effects=list(c(s_index,list(Intercept=1),list(covariate))),
                         tag="pred")

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Using Inla with SPDE approach
parts:
Hi,
In order to predict at new locations, you need all the inputs of the model at those locations, and that includes the values of all the covariates you used to build the model.
If you don’t have the values of covariates, sometimes an option is to explicitly model the missing covariate values; for example, if a covariate is a slowly varying function of space, then you might build a spatial model for it, and include it in your overall model.
I believe there are such multivariate models among the spde examples on r-inla.org.

Finn
